tags.why: Al Jazeera on 2026-10-26 reports the worst month for ships in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran warned the US Navy as fears of renewed war grew, so war-risk premiums and transit delays are continuing.
tags.action: Ask your forwarder for current war-risk surcharges on Gulf-bound cargo and hold 10 to 14 days of buffer stock for anything that must transit Hormuz.

tags.why: Houthi attacks are escalating again as of 2026-10-26, prompting Egypt to approve military aid for Saudi Arabia, so Red Sea shipping faces strikes and continued diversions.
tags.action: Keep Asia-Europe cargo routed via the Cape of Good Hope and ask your carrier to confirm in writing whether any Red Sea transit is planned and what the surcharge is.

tags.why: Fresh Houthi strikes reported on 2026-10-26 keep Bab el-Mandeb a high-threat chokepoint, so carriers are still avoiding it or charging heavy war-risk premiums.
tags.action: Confirm with your forwarder that no booking is planned through Bab el-Mandeb, and budget for Cape routing at 10 to 14 extra days.

tags.why: Escalating Houthi attacks and the Saudi-Houthi conflict as of 2026-10-26 keep carriers away from the Red Sea, so Suez Canal transits stay depressed or are diverted around Africa.
tags.action: Plan Asia-Europe and Asia-Mediterranean lanes with Cape of Good Hope transit times and ask your forwarder for a Suez-versus-Cape rate comparison.

tags.why: Hormuz tensions and fears of renewed US-Israel strikes on Iran (2026-10-26) threaten the shipping lane that serves Jebel Ali, which could mean congestion, delays and surcharges.
tags.action: Ask your forwarder about a fallback via Khor Fakkan or Fujairah with onward trucking, and pre-book it for time-critical Gulf deliveries.

tags.why: With Trump weighing a deal or to 'finish it off' and Iran warning the US Navy on 2026-10-26, renewed strikes could close Iranian airspace to cargo flights again.
tags.action: Ask your air forwarder to pre-plan routings that avoid Iranian airspace, with extra fuel-stop time built into Asia-Europe schedules.

tags.why: Fears of renewed fighting between Israel and Iran (2026-10-26), including an IDF debate over a pre-election operation, could close Israeli, Lebanese and Jordanian airspace at short notice.
tags.action: Ask your air carrier for alternative routings and cancellation terms on cargo flights over the Levant.
